To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the performance of transfer metric learning for action recognition depends on the type of transfer and that a hierarchical knowledge representation is beneficial for the task of learning transferable metric spaces.

(1) different transfer types are influenced by the semantic knowledge representation, and (2) a hierarchical knowledge representation based on the embedded semantic structure is more effective in transfer metric learning than a flat knowledge representation.

(1) transfer learning for action similarity is a challenging problem, and that (2) the proposed hierarchical transfer metric learning framework is able to improve the performance of the action similarity task.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the transfer of knowledge from source domains to novel domains.
the following questions: (1) How to learn a transferable metric from a source domain to a target domain? (2) How to learn an adaptive metric for the source and the target domain, respectively?
the question of how to transfer high-level semantic knowledge to improve the performance of action similarity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
transfer learning is an effective way to learn classifiers that generalize well even in challenging domains.

our approach outperforms all baselines in the majority of the transfer scenarios, which demonstrates the effectiveness of transfer metric learning in the context of learning classifiers for action similarity.
our proposed transfer metric learning framework is able to improve the performance of the base learner on the novel domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the interplay between knowledge representation and knowledge transfer type is of crucial importance.

we have shown that the interdependence between high-level knowledge representations and knowledge transfer methods has a significant effect on the performance of the resulting classifier in a novel domain, and thus should be considered carefully when designing a transfer learning system.
we study the effect of various knowledge representations and transfer types in the context of transfer metric learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of transfer method is crucial for the success of knowledge transfer.
knowledge transfer can improve the performance of metric learning in challenging settings.

transfer metric learning is not only useful for improving the performance in challenging learning scenarios, but it can also be used to improve the robustness of transfer learning methods against negative transfer by choosing the right knowledge representation for the given transfer type.
